Capability final class

Snapshot of the detected terminal's image-rendering capabilities. Immutable value object returned by Detect::probe().

MethodSummary
static universal(?CellSize $cellSize = null, bool $inTmux = false): selfBuild a full-capability instance (all protocols available). Used for Mosaic::halfBlock() which is always available.
static kitty(?CellSize $cellSize = null, bool $inTmux = false): selfKitty-only capability built from an environment claim: the env hypothesis, not a confirmed result. Detect::probe() keeps it only when the terminal answers the APC a=q query, and Detect::fromEnv() reports the claim unconfirmed. A caller that builds it directly asserts Kitty on the environment alone, so it must not treat the result as a confirmed Kitty terminal.
static iterm2(?CellSize $cellSize = null, bool $inTmux = false): selfiTerm2-only capability.
static sixel(?CellSize $cellSize = null, bool $inTmux = false): selfSixel-only capability.
static unknown(?CellSize $cellSize = null, bool $inTmux = false): selfEmpty capability set — used when no probe data is available.
withCellSize(?CellSize $cellSize): selfReturn a copy of this capability with the given cell size attached. Used by Detect::probeFontSize() to attach font-size data to whatever protocol was detected via env vars or DA1. A null $cellSize means "size unknown" — the probe never measured one — which is also the never-set state: renderers fall back to their own cell assumptions for it, so no sentinel distinction exists.
withDefaultColors(?string $defaultFg, ?string $defaultBg): selfReturn a copy of this capability with the terminal's reported default colours attached (lowercase 'rrggbb', null keeps unknown), shaped exactly like withCellSize() — the OSC 10/11 answers ride onto whichever protocol rung the ladder answered on.
withTerminalFacts(?int $quirks, string $passthroughMode): selfReturn a copy carrying the terminal-database facts — the quirks bitmask (null = chain never consulted, the byte-frozen shape) and the passthrough envelope mode. Built by Detect::probeEnv() on the resolved TermInfo, mirroring how chafa consults chafa_term_info_get_quirks() at the output epilogue (chafa.c:445-451) and dispatches on the chained passthrough mode (chafa-passthrough-encoder.c:145-165).
detectSummary(): stringReturn a human-readable summary of which protocols were detected. Mirrors Charmbracelet's image.(Kitty|Sixel|Iterm2|HalfBlock)Protocol.Name().

static cached(): CapabilityProbe once and cache the result for the lifetime of this process.
static fromEnv(?array $env = null): CapabilityClassify the terminal from environment variables alone: no tty, no query bytes, no timeout, no tmux process. Pure, so it can run in a test, in a pipeline, or before the program has a tty at all.

static setProbeStdin($fd): voidOverride the stdin source used during DA1 probing. Use this in tests to inject canned responses.
static setProbeStdout($stream): voidOverride the stdout sink used for writing the queries. Use this in tests to capture the query bytes the probe sends instead of spraying them onto the process's real STDOUT (finding 031); production code leaves this null. Pass null to restore the real STDOUT. Like setProbeStdin(), a test seam, not a knob.
static setAutoPassthrough(bool $enabled): voidOpt the automatic tmux allow-passthrough transaction on or off . Default on; TmuxPassthrough::ensure() consults this on every call. Takes effect immediately for future probes — an already-open transaction is NOT rolled back here; retire it via TmuxPassthrough::retire().
static autoPassthrough(): boolWhether setAutoPassthrough() currently permits the auto-toggle transaction.
static supportsRepeat(): boolCapability gate: does the current terminal interpret ESC[count b (REP — repeat the preceding graphic character)?
static setSupportsRepeatOverride(?bool $supported): voidForce the REP answer for tests (null restores the env table). Same shape as the other Detect tri-states: while overridden, the table below is never consulted.
static clearSupportsRepeatOverride(): voidRemove the override; supportsRepeat() goes back to the env table.
static setTmuxTermFeaturesOverride(?bool $state): voidForce the tmux termfeatures answer for tests: true = outer terminal has sixel, false = definite no (veto), null = AUTO (the fail-soft verdict — while overridden, NO tmux process is ever spawned).
static clearTmuxTermFeaturesOverride(): voidRemove the override; probeTmuxTermFeatures() goes back to asking tmux.
static setTerminfoSixelOverride(bool $present): voidTest seam: pin the terminfo sixl answer without touching a real terminal database. true = short-circuit the ladder to sixel; false = "terminfo says nothing", fall through to the DA1 arm. While overridden no infocmp process is ever spawned.
static clearTerminfoSixelOverride(): voidRemove the override; probeTerminfoSixel() consults the live probe again.
static setTerminfoProbe(?TerminalProbe $probe): voidSeam: substitute the TerminalProbe the live arm runs (null restores default construction). The capability table itself stays in sugar-colorprofile — this is wiring, not a second lookup.

ImageLayer final class

A per-frame registry that turns pixel-graphics blobs into tiling-safe cell blocks and collects them for a \SugarCraft\Core\View's image layer.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly ?Renderer $renderer = null)
renderer(): ?RendererThe renderer delete sequences are drawn from, or null when the layer was constructed without one (release()/releaseAllExcept() then still un-register placements but report empty sequences).
static digestFor(string $bytes, int $width, int $height): stringWindow key for a placement: content hash over bytes + cell footprint.
place(string $bytes, int $width, int $height): stringRegister $bytes and return a $width × $height marker block to drop in the frame (or a blank block of the same size once the id space is full). Deduplicates by content, so repeated bytes reuse their id.
placeTracked(string $bytes, int $width, int $height): PlacedImageplace(), but also reporting the overlay id the bytes were assigned.
placements(): arrayThe accumulated image layer (id → ImagePlacement) to hand to a \SugarCraft\Core\View. The runtime paints only the markers a given frame actually contains, so over-registering (e.g. images scrolled out of view) is harmless.
removeById(int $imageId): voidRemove a placement by its image id.
trackedDigests(): arrayEvery window digest currently tracked (one per distinct bytes+size combination that has been placed), in first-seen order.
imageIdForDigest(string $digest): ?intThe image id a window digest is currently placed under, or null when it has never been placed, was since removed/released, or the id was re-placed at a different footprint (last-footprint-wins, see placeTracked()). Lets a viewport check its scratch digest against the layer before deciding to re-fetch/re-render — a null here after a size change is the layer telling you to re-place.
release(int $imageId): stringFree one image: drop its placement (and its window-digest tracking) and return the escape sequence that deletes its terminal-side allocation. The bytes forfeit their id claim too — this door, not removeById, is where the id space is reclaimed (lowestFreeId()). Unknown id → no-op, empty string.
releaseAllExcept(array $keepIds): arrayViewport windowing: free every placement whose id is NOT in $keepIds and return the delete sequences to emit, keyed by released image id.
isEmpty(): bool

static chafa(string ...$options): selfForce the Chafa renderer with optional CLI options.
static symbols(CanvasMode $canvas = CanvasMode::TrueColor, float $workFactor = SymbolMapRenderer::DEFAULT_WORK_FACTOR, ?string $symbols = null): selfForce the coverage-class symbol-map renderer.
withCanvasMode(CanvasMode $canvasMode): selfSwitch the colour canvas when the active backend is a text-tier renderer that speaks CanvasModeConfigurable (SymbolMapRenderer, QuarterBlockRenderer — also through a passthrough envelope); returns the same instance otherwise.
withSymbolSelectors(string $selectors): selfSelect the symbol corpus with chafa's --symbols= tag grammar when the active backend is the symbol-map renderer (also through a passthrough envelope); same instance otherwise. An invalid expression throws — never a silently empty corpus.
withWorkFactor(float $workFactor): selfForward chafa's --work dial when the active backend speaks WorkFactorConfigurable; same instance otherwise.
withDither(Dither $dither): selfReturn a new Mosaic with a different dither algorithm. Only meaningful when the current renderer is a SixelRenderer (also through a passthrough envelope); returns the same instance otherwise.
acceptsDither(): boolWhether the live backend hears the dither dial at all (withDither() and the builder's dither/sixel dials take effect). Answered through a passthrough envelope.
acceptsCanvasMode(): boolWhether the live backend speaks CanvasModeConfigurable — i.e. withCanvasMode() has an ear.
acceptsWorkFactor(): boolWhether the live backend speaks WorkFactorConfigurable — i.e. withWorkFactor() has an ear.
acceptsSymbolSelectors(): boolWhether the live backend is the symbol-map renderer whose chafa --symbols= corpus withSymbolSelectors() selects.
ignoredDials(): arrayThe dial categories the live backend cannot hear, in the fixed order dither, canvasMode, workFactor, symbolSelectors. The tuning doors are silent no-ops on backends without an ear (the silence-law of this facade); this is their consultation surface — a doctor panel or the candy-code route asks which knobs would be ignored BEFORE offering them, instead of letting a user tune a dead dial. An empty list means every dial is live.
withOptimization(Optimization ...$levels): selfReturn a new Mosaic configured with optimization levels (chafa CHAFA_OPTIMIZATIONS ladder parity).
optimizations(): intThe currently configured Optimization mask (0 = None).
capability(): CapabilityExpose the detected capability snapshot.
protocol(): stringStable backend name: 'sixel' | 'kitty' | 'iterm2' | 'halfblock' | 'quarterblock' | 'ascii' | 'chafa' | 'symbols'. This slot names the PROTOCOL only. The three AsciiRenderer colour arms all report 'ascii' here — pair with modeDetail() wherever the encoded bytes must be told apart.
modeDetail(): ?stringExtra discriminator for when protocol() alone does not identify the encoded bytes. AsciiRenderer has four colour arms behind one protocol name, so an Ansi16/Ansi256/TrueColor ascii mosaic reports its AsciiColorMode value ('ansi16'/'ansi256'/'truecolor') here; every other renderer — and the Mono ascii arm, whose protocol name already is its mode value — reports null. A passthrough-decorated mosaic answers for its inner renderer, the same way the decorator's 'tmux(<inner>)'/'screen(<inner>)' name does.
renderer(): RendererThe renderer this mosaic encodes through (tmux decorator included when the terminal runs under tmux).
static supportedProtocols(): arrayAll protocols supported by this library, in preferred order.
isInline(): boolTrue if render() produces inline cell text that can be placed directly in a text frame (half/quarter-block, ASCII); false for a pixel-graphics blob (Sixel/Kitty/iTerm2) that must be painted as an out-of-band overlay. See Renderer::isInline().
fontSize(): ?arrayBest-effort font-size derived from capability detection. Returns null if font-size probing hasn't been implemented yet.
scale(): ?ScaleThe configured scale mode, or null for the default (Fit).
render(ImageSource $image, ?int $width = null, ?int $height = null): stringRender the image to ANSI bytes at the given cell dimensions.
renderRows(ImageSource $image, int $width, ?int $height = null): \GeneratorRow-lazy twin of render(): the SAME scale pipeline runs up front (including its throws), then the encoded bytes arrive as append-order chunks whose concatenation is exactly what render() would have returned.
static builder(): MosaicBuilderBuilder for fine-grained configuration.
withScale(Scale $scale): selfSet the scale mode for rendering.
adaptive(ImageSource $image): AdaptiveImageCreate a memoizing AdaptiveImage for the given source.
precompute(ImageSource $image, int $width, ?int $height = null): PrecomputedImageRender and cache one specific size as a PrecomputedImage.
static fromModeString(string $mode, bool $probe = true): ?selfBuild a Mosaic from a render-mode string.
poster(string $url, int $cellW, ?int $cellH = null, ?DiskCache $cache = null, ?array $allowedHosts = null): stringFetch a poster image from $url and render it at cell size in one call, consulting and populating an optional on-disk render cache.
posterAsync(string $url, int $cellW, ?int $cellH = null, ?DiskCache $cache = null, ?array $allowedHosts = null): PromiseInterfaceAsync variant of poster() — resolves with the rendered bytes.
posterFile(string $path, int $cellW, ?int $cellH = null, ?DiskCache $cache = null): stringRender a poster that already lives on local disk, with the same Fill-by-default scaling and optional DiskCache windowing as poster(). The cache key is derived from $path in place of a URL — and, unlike the URL legs, from the file's CURRENT identity (mtime at nanosecond resolution + size, finding 034): a remote URL is an immutable-enough handle for a TTL-free memo, but a path is a promise that the bytes under it never change, and they do. An edited or replaced poster therefore self-invalidates on the next call instead of serving the old encode forever under a stable key. Entries for since-deleted generations age out through the normal eviction cap; a stat failure (file vanished mid-call) falls back to the bare path — fromFile() is about to throw anyway.

PngMetadata final class

PNG container codec for the A1111 infotext round-trip — no SD server, no library, pure byte work over the chunk framing of ISO/IEC 15948.

MethodSummary
static isPng(string $bytes): boolMagic sniff: eight fixed signature bytes, nothing more.
static readText(string $pngBytes, string $keyword = self::KEYWORD_PARAMETERS): ?stringExtract the text stored under $keyword, or null for ANY unfavourable shape: not a PNG, oversized, truncated tail, CRC-mismatched chunk, malformed text chunk, compressed iTXt that will not inflate (including one that would inflate past MAX_TEXT_BYTES), a text payload over that ceiling, or simply absent keyword. Never throws (reader resilience law).
static writeText(string $pngBytes, string $keyword, string $text, ?string &$strategy = null): stringReturn the PNG with $keyword carrying $text: an existing tEXt/iTXt chunk with that keyword is REPLACED in place — never appended as a duplicate — and every other chunk keeps its bytes and ordering untouched, including trailing bytes after IEND. No matching chunk → a new one is inserted immediately before IEND.
static setInfotext(string $pngBytes, string $text): stringStamp the full infotext block: $text becomes the parameters chunk (in place, per the replacement law) and an already-present prompt chunk is re-synced to the first line of the text — the A1111 pair law ("parameters" tEXt carries everything, "prompt" iTXt carries the bare prompt). A file without a prompt chunk is not given one: the minimal-diff / preservation law outranks minting upstream's newer companion chunk on our stamps.
static stamp(string $pngBytes, string $text): stringStamp an infotext block into a PNG (pure byte transform): $text becomes the parameters chunk and an existing prompt chunk is re-synced to the text's first line. Alias of setInfotext().
static extract(string $pngBytes): arrayRead both A1111 keywords at once. A missing keyword, or any damaged / non-PNG input, yields null for that entry; never throws.
static strategyFor(string $text): stringStrategy law in one place (W1.7 step 2): ASCII rides tEXt; non-ASCII that is legal UTF-8 rides compressed iTXt; raw 8-bit bytes that are not valid UTF-8 (a legacy latin-1 dump) ride tEXt verbatim — exactly "A1111 writes tEXt with the raw str", since iTXt text must be UTF-8.

Renderer interface

Contract for image-to-terminal renderers.

MethodSummary
render(ImageSource $image, int $width, ?int $height = null): stringRender $image into ANSI bytes at the given cell dimensions.
name(): stringStable backend identifier: 'sixel' | 'kitty' | 'iterm2' | 'chafa' | 'halfblock' | 'quarterblock' | 'ascii' | 'symbols'.
supportsAlpha(): boolTrue if this backend supports partial transparency (alpha channel). The graphics tiers (Sixel, Kitty, iTerm2, Chafa) do; the text tiers (half-block, quarter-block, ASCII, symbol map) do not.
isInline(): boolTrue if render() produces inline cell text — newline-separated rows, one terminal line per cell row — that can be placed directly in a text frame and stitched beside other content (half-block, quarter-block, ASCII, symbol map, and Chafa).

renderRgb(string $rgba, int $pixelWidth, int $pixelHeight, int $width, ?int $height = null): stringRender a raw straight-alpha RGBA8 buffer (\SugarCraft\Image\Codec\RawRgba layout: $pixelWidth × $pixelHeight × 4 bytes, rows top to bottom).
present(ImageSource $image, int $width, ?int $height, string $imageId, ?string $prevId): stringEmit one frame of a sequence that may be re-displayed later.
supportsIdDelete(): boolTrue when delete() removes one specific frame by its id, so a replaced frame can be retired after the new one is on screen. Kitty only: iTerm2's delete pops the topmost image and Sixel has no delete at all.

SixelRenderer final class

Sixel graphics renderer — DEC sixel to terminal.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly Dither $dither = Dither::FloydSteinberg, private readonly int $maxColors = 256, private readonly int $cellWidth = 10, private readonly int $cellHeight = 20, ?float $intensity = null, private readonly int $alphaThreshold = self::DEFAULT_ALPHA_THRESHOLD, private readonly ?Color $flattenBackground = null, private readonly bool $serpentine = false, private readonly bool $mltermEdgeRows = false, private readonly ?int $quality = null, private readonly bool $autoLevels = false, private readonly ?int $quirks = null)
render(ImageSource $image, int $width, ?int $height = null): string
encodeBandStream(ImageSource $image, int $width, callable $write, ?int $height = null): voidStream the Sixel encoding one 6-pixel-tall band at a time.
name(): string
supportsAlpha(): boolSixel supports transparent backgrounds via the #0;2;P background register: fully-transparent pixels are left unpainted and show the terminal's own background. See render().
isInline(): bool
delete(string $imageId): stringSixel has no standard delete mechanism — DECSIXEL does not support removing individual images after emission. Returns the empty string.
dither(): Dither
configFingerprint(): stringEvery ctor config that changes the encoded bytes rides the fingerprint — dither arms the index grid differently, maxColors changes the palette, and the cell-pixel geometry resamples to a different pixel canvas, so two SixelRenderers named 'sixel' with any of these differing must never cross-serve a poster cache entry.
withDither(Dither $dither): selfA copy of this renderer using $dither, keeping its colour budget, bias intensity and cell-pixel geometry — so re-tinting a configured Sixel (custom maxColors or real terminal cell sizes) never silently resets them.
withIntensity(?float $intensity): selfA copy of this renderer using $intensity as its dither bias, keeping the dither algorithm, color budget and cell geometry. Refusals come from the constructor's own grammar (NaN and negatives rejected by name); values above 1.0 clamp to full bias, and null releases the tuning entirely — back to the chafa-config default ladder, the byte-frozen legacy shape.
withMaxColors(int $maxColors): selfA copy of this renderer quantising its palette to at most $maxColors entries — same keep-everything-else contract as withDither(); out-of-range budgets are refused by the constructor ladder before any copy exists.
alphaThreshold(): intThe GD-alpha hole cut-off in force (0..127; 127 = only fully transparent pixels are holes, the older behaviour).
flattenBackground(): ?ColorThe flatten background in force, or null when semi-transparent pixels keep their stored colour.
withAlphaThreshold(int $threshold): selfCopy with a different alpha threshold: pixels whose GD alpha reaches $threshold become background holes, and the hole decision happens before the pixel ever enters the palette census or the diffusion stream (chafa quantize_pixel skip semantics, chafa/internal/chafa-indexed-image.c:117-125 — lowered thresholds also shed semi-transparent fringe colours from median-cut buckets, the counterpart of chafa's MAX(alpha_threshold,1) sampler guard). 127 is byte-identical to the historical === 127 hole test; the extreme 0 declares every pixel (opaque included) a hole — legal, but the encode paints nothing.
withFlatten(?Color $background): selfOpt-in pre-sampling flatten — every semi-transparent pixel (0 < alpha < threshold) is composited toward $background inside the base read, BEFORE quantisation or diffusion touch it, so the encoder dithers the colour the terminal will actually show instead of the raw un-premultiplied fringe (which is typically near-black — the dark-halo defect). null (default) disables flattening entirely.
serpentine(): boolTrue when the diffusion walk snakes (odd rows reversed).
withSerpentine(bool $serpentine = true): selfCopy with the serpentine scan armed. Only diffusion dithers are affected — Ordered is a position-taken bias and None has no walk to reverse, so both render byte-identically with or without it.
mltermEdgeRows(): boolTrue when the mlterm first/last-row quirk is armed.
withMltermEdgeRows(bool $mltermEdgeRows = true): selfCopy with the mlterm edge-band quirk armed. The quirk only ever fires on a canvas that carries the transparent background register (offset 1) whose global first or last band encodes to nothing at all; those bands then draw a full-width zero-bit run on register 0 so the graphics position advances across the whole row. Off by default until the TermDb table can select it per terminal.
withCellSize(int $cellWidth, int $cellHeight): selfCopy sized to a probed terminal cell rather than the constructor's conventional 10×20.
withQuirks(?int $quirks): selfCopy armed from a terminal-database quirks bitmask (TermInfo::QUIRK_*). Two chicle consumers re-home here: QUIRK_MLTERM_EDGE_ROWS arms the full-width edge-band forcing (the flag's "auto-enabling belongs to the TermDb capability table" home promised in its docblock), and the ABSENCE of QUIRK_SIXEL_OVERSHOOT on a KNOWN terminal makes the encoder append the parking newline chafa writes at chafa.c:445-451 — a terminal with the quirk parks its own cursor a row below the final band and needs nothing extra. Passing QUIRK_NONE is a positive fact ("chain consulted, no quirks") and still earns the parking newline; only the never-polled null default keeps the legacy bytes frozen.
quirks(): ?intThe armed quirks mask, null when the terminal was never consulted (the byte-frozen default).
hasQuirk(int $quirk): boolWhether one QUIRK_* bit is armed. Null quirks answers false for every bit — no facts, no quirk-driven bytes.
parkingNewline(): stringThe parking newline chafa.c:445-451 appends after sixel output when the terminal is KNOWN not to overshoot its cursor. Returns '' for the frozen null default and for overshooting terminals.
quality(): ?intThe PNN quality rung in force (1-9), or null when the renderer quantises with median-cut — the byte-frozen default.
autoLevels(): boolChafa's --preprocessing auto-levels in force — the fast-intensity histogram bounds, per-channel stretch, and Rec.709 saturation lift run before the palette census (see LevelsStretch()). Default OFF: every byte-frozen digest predates the pass.
withAutoLevels(bool $autoLevels = true): selfA copy using (or not using) the auto-levels pass, keeping every other dial.
withQuality(int $quality): selfCopy on a different rung of the chafa -w ladder (1-9). Arming it routes palette construction through Quantizer when the sample census outweighs the colour budget; every other setting rides along. The default path never calls this, so default bytes are untouched.
maxColors(): intThe maximum number of colors in the quantized Sixel palette.
intensity(): ?floatThe Ordered/Noise dither bias in force (0.0..1.0), or null when the renderer runs the chafa-config default ladder untouched.
renderRgb(string $rgba, int $pixelWidth, int $pixelHeight, int $width, ?int $height = null): string
present(ImageSource $image, int $width, ?int $height, string $imageId, ?string $prevId): string
supportsIdDelete(): bool

WorkFactorConfigurable interface

Optional capability: the renderer exposes chafa's work-effort dial — 0.0 spends the least per cell (single best Hamming candidate), 1.0 scores the whole corpus. Same interface-cannot-have- bodies rationale as CanvasModeConfigurable: Mosaic delegates only when the active backend declares this.

SymbolDef final class

One candidate glyph of the coverage-class corpus: its character, the 8x8 coverage it paints packed row-major MSB-first into a 64-bit bitmap (pixel (x,y) = bit 63-(y*8+x)), the family tags, and the precomputed foreground weight (popcount) — chafa stores exactly this on every ChafaSymbol and the scoring path divides the foreground group by it without re-counting (chafa/internal/chafa-symbols.c calc_weights).

SymbolMap final class

Coverage-class symbol engine — the glyph corpus and candidate search behind the 'symbols' render tier.

MethodSummary
static new(): self
withLatin(): selfOpt-in LATIN tier: chafa's 365 narrow chafa-symbols-latin.h glyphs (U+00A1-U+03F6, table SymbolSetLatin) appended after the current corpus.
hasLatin(): boolWhether the opt-in LATIN tier is appended (see withLatin()).
withAsciiIbm(): selfSwap the ascii tier (U+0020–U+007E) to chafa's orphaned IBM face — the verbatim chafa-symbols-ascii-ibm.h transcription in SymbolSetTables::ASCII_IBM.
hasAsciiIbm(): boolWhether the ascii tier carries the IBM face (see withAsciiIbm()).
withKana(): selfOpt-in KANA wide tier: chafa's 181 16x8 chafa-symbols-kana.h glyphs (U+3041-U+30FE, table SymbolSetKana) appended after the current wide selection as chafa's wide symbols2 pairs (WideSymbolDef) — never the narrow corpus.
hasKana(): boolWhether the opt-in KANA wide tier is appended (see withKana()).
wideDefs(): arrayThe map's wide (two-cell) selection in build order — chafa's symbols2 array. Empty on every narrow-only map, so the wide render pass never activates for the default corpus or the latin/ascii-ibm tiers.
wideCorpus(): arrayThe wide selection in chafa's symbols2 scan order — joint popcount ascending, ties by codepoint ascending (findWideCandidates() narrows inside the same order; the renderer's exhaustive path walks it directly, so ties resolve exactly like the C's init-sorted array).
defs(): arrayThe corpus in build order (basic, braille, sextant, octant) — then the opt-in LATIN tier when withLatin() was used.
hasSymbol(int $codepoint): boolchafa_symbol_map_has_symbol (chafa-symbol-map.c:1137): whether the selection holds a codepoint. The solid-cell shortcut consults it for U+2588 (see \SugarCraft\Image\Renderer\SymbolMapRenderer's solid ladder).
withSelectors(string $selectors): selfApply chafa's --symbols= tag selector grammar over the FULL corpus — the narrow array (1,260 unique glyphs) and the wide symbols2 array (181 kana glyphs) — returning a new map holding each selection in its corpus build order.
findCandidates(int $bitmap, bool $allowInverse, int $limit): arraychafa's find_candidates(): a flat popcount-Hamming walk of every corpus bitmap maintaining an insertion-sorted window of the eight best (symbol, inverted) trials. Equal distances keep scan order; an inverse trial (64 - hd) rides the same buffer.
findWideCandidates(int $bitmapLeft, int $bitmapRight, bool $allowInverse, int $limit): arrayChafa's find_wide_candidates (chafa-symbol-map.c:1268) — the same 8-slot insertion buffer over the WIDE selection, but the distance is the joint hamming of the two 8x8 halves against the candidate's sym[0]/sym[1] pair, seeded at hd 129 with the inverse trial at 128 - hd. The scan order is chafa's own: compare_symbols2_popcount sorts symbols2 ascending by joint weight then codepoint (stable across equal keys), not build order — the wide array is sorted at init in the C, and this port keeps that law so ties resolve exactly like chafa's.
static coverageToBitmap(array $coverage, ?int $threshold = null): intchafa coverage_to_bitmap(): row-major MSB-first packing of the 8x8 coverage, pixel (x,y) landing on bit 63-(y*8+x). Two faces: the corpus generators (outline 255/0, braille/sextant/octant 1/0) use the truthy form exactly like chafa's internal one; the runtime conversion of a 0..255 pixel ramp passes $threshold = 127 (chafa/chafa-symbol-map.c:240) — the single place the 8-bit ramp becomes binary.
static coverageOf(int $bitmap): arraychafa bitmap_to_bytes(): the binary coverage bytes painted by a bitmap, index = y*8+x (the same bit order as coverageToBitmap).

SymbolSetKana final class

KANA: the wide 16x8 kana symbol tier — chafa's chafa-symbols-kana.h table.

SymbolSetLatin final class

The LATIN symbol set — chafa's chafa-symbols-latin.h table: 365 narrow 8x8 glyphs spanning U+00A1-U+03F6 (Latin-1 supplement, Latin Extended-A and -B, IPA extensions, spacing modifier letters, Greek), transcribed one row per glyph as 'row|row|...' ('X' = painted pixel, MSB-first like SymbolMap::coverageToBitmap()). The bitmaps are chafa's own, a close match to the Terminus ter-x14n font (chafa-symbols-latin.h header).

SymbolSetTables final class

The chafa narrow symbol tables this port had not yet carried: the ASCII glyph set (U+0020–U+007E), its orphaned alternate face ASCII_IBM, the Latin/Greek set (U+00A1–U+03F6), the misc-narrow set (U+2190–U+25FC) and the "Symbols for Legacy Computing" block entries of chafa's block table (U+1FB3C–U+1FBAE) that are neither the generated sextant range nor the eighth-block tier.

Coverage-class symbol tags, bit-for-bit mirrors of chafa's ChafaSymbolTag enum. Tags classify a glyph's visual family; defs ride their table declarations and SymbolMap::withSelectors() filters on the effective tags exactly as chafa's char_is_selected() does — the old "selection never filters" v1 note predates the selector grammar), also serving callers that want to restrict a pick to, say, BRAILLE or STIPPLE families.

WideSymbolDef final class

One candidate WIDE glyph of the coverage-class corpus — chafa's ChafaSymbol2: a 16x8-pixel cell carried as TWO 8x8 bitmaps (sym[0] the left half, sym[1] the right half), each packed row-major MSB-first like SymbolDef::$bits, scored jointly as hd(left) + hd(right) against the two canvas cells it would replace (chafa/internal/chafa-symbols.c init_symbol_array_wide: left = def_to_symbol offset 0 rowstride 16, right = offset 8).
